transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. I understand we've been offered a block of distressed municipal bonds with a face value of $12 million, currently quoted at 82 cents on the dollar, maturing in 30 months. As chair of the Risk Committee, I'll be making the binding decision on whether we proceed and on what conditions. Before I record the vote, I need to hear from each of the four required functions under our normal pre-trade procedure: credit risk, legal, markets, and accounting. Please state any conditions or implementation requirements you have. I'll record the vote immediately after the last of those four has spoken. Who would like to begin?

transcript.text: I need to flag an important exposure issue before we proceed. I confirmed in the exposure report I reviewed this morning that the bank already has $4,000,000 of exposure to this issuer, and the applicable single-issuer limit is $10,000,000. This position has not yet been added to the committee packet. This means that if we purchase the full $12 million face value of these bonds, our total exposure to this issuer would reach $16 million, which would exceed our single-issuer limit by $6 million. As a credit risk condition, we would need to either reduce the purchase size to stay within the $10 million limit, or obtain an exception to the single-issuer limit before proceeding.

transcript.text: During my review of the bond terms this week, I determined that the contractual cash flows include a contingent step-up feature. This means the position must be recorded at fair value through profit or loss rather than held at amortized cost. My accounting memo on this finding is awaiting circulation. As an accounting implementation requirement, the trade tickets and downstream systems must be set up to classify and measure this position at fair value through profit or loss from inception, not at amortized cost.

The position must be classified and measured at fair value through profit or loss from inception, not at amortized cost, due to the contingent step-up feature in the contractual cash flows.
The total purchase must be sized at exactly $5,000,000 face value executed over exactly four trading days in a single cycle, consistent with the desk's $5,000,000 per-cycle maximum.
Total issuer exposure must remain at or below the $10,000,000 single-issuer limit. With $4,000,000 existing exposure and $5,000,000 new purchase, total exposure will be $9,000,000, within the limit.
